summary: Verified src/sig/api.py::encoder_parameters, ::warm_up and ::cadence_due -- the three bodies committed unverified -- against a real spine.assemble.build() config, calling them together with src/opt/api.py::build. AST-walked src/spine/compose.py::compose: four sig_api call sites, and encoder_parameters (compose.py L2007) and warm_up (L2047) are BOTH UNGUARDED -- only load_state_dict sits behind `if 'SIG' in saved`. cadence_due is not called from compose() at all; it is a LOOP_ORDER row. THE INTERFACE TO OPT IS SOUND: encoder_parameters returns a plain list of the same 3 nn.Parameter objects as st.encoder.parameters() (identity-checked), compose wraps it in list() under the key 'encoder', opt/api.py::build accepts exactly {'base','encoder'} and builds enc_opt over ordered[1][1] -- proven by id-set equality between the returned params and the encoder AdamW's param_groups, a real backward+step that moved emb.weight/proj.weight/proj.bias by 2.0e-3 each, and zero movement on the base group. The bigram arm returns [] and OPT counts the empty group (opt.build.params.encoder=0) rather than refusing it. warm_up uses the NAMED field: compose passes opt=sysm.optimizer.encoder and the body only calls opt.zero_grad/backward/step on it -- 800 steps moved the encoder (emb 0.187, proj 0.356, bias 0.013), moved the base parameter by exactly 0.0, populated 3 AdamW state entries on the encoder and 0 on the base, and left every .grad None. RNG IS CLEAN, NO FIFTH COLLISION: exactly two torch.Generator mints in the whole package (api.py L161 in build, L750 in warm_up), each seeded from one .randint() off the declared stream; zero rng_for, zero .spawn(), zero .torch_generator(), zero global seeding -- rng.issued() is unchanged across warm_up, the sig stream advanced 1->2 draws, and torch's global RNG state is bit-identical before and after. ENCODER WIDTH IS STILL AT THE SLOT CEILING: nothing in the three bodies reads a vocabulary at all; verified at SIG_SPACE=tokens that emb rows = LM.vocab_slots = 4096 while warming over a 300-id live stream, and width_units is read only from SigState. TWO DEFECTS FOUND. (1) HIGH, at shipped defaults: the 'collapsing' run-level-failure verdict CANNOT be produced, because _stop_verdict is behind `len(curve) < 2` while SIG_WARMUP=800 / SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=500 admits exactly ONE probe -- a fully collapsed encoder (separation -0.000000, threshold 0.15) returns verdict='budget', and the UNREACHABLE gate's own reason sentence tells the operator the opposite in as many words. (2) MEDIUM: cadence_due seeds sig.cadence_idle only in its not-due branch, so at the shipped SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=1 every dense check is due and the key is ABSENT -- KeyError, not the 0 its own DID IT FIRE block says means 'the gate never left the dense arm'. Three further low findings on reason-sentence accuracy. LEVERS READ is exact in both directions for all three functions and every DID IT FIRE name is produced. SIG DEFAULTS (18 levers, 1 wire): SIG_MODE=learned (learned|bigram), SIG_SPACE=bytes (bytes|tokens), SIG_D=64, SIG_BIGRAM_DIM=512, SIG_CONTRASTIVE_BATCH=48, SIG_TEMP=0.1, SIG_POSITIVE_RADIUS_WINDOWS=2.0, SIG_PROTOTYPE_FRAC=0.0 (OFF, and structurally unreachable -- no DOM reservoir supplier), SIG_FLOOR_KINDS=8, SIG_VAR_WEIGHT=5.0 (ON), SIG_COV_WEIGHT=0.0 (OFF), SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=1, SIG_TRAIN_EVERY_IDLE=12, SIG_DENSE_WINDOW=400, SIG_WARMUP=800, SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC=0.25, SIG_WARMUP_PLATEAU_EPS=0.015, SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=500; wire SIG.d_idle_cadence = max(train_every*6, train_every_idle) = 12 at defaults. WHAT IS OFF AT DEFAULTS: the covariance term, the prototype arm, and -- as of finding 1 -- the entire adaptive warm-up stop INCLUDING its collapse verdict. Five SIG entry points remain NotImplementedError stubs (train_step, counters, state_dict, load_state_dict, encoder_embedding), which is expected. No file under src/ was edited; the only working-tree modification is src/data/api.py, which belongs to another agent.

findings.detail: At the SHIPPED DEFAULTS the 'collapsing' verdict -- which warm_up's own docstring calls 'a RUN-LEVEL FAILURE' and 'what the composition root has to act on itself' -- cannot be produced, and the gate that reports the mechanism asserts in writing that it can. SIG_WARMUP=800 with SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=500 puts exactly ONE probe in the budget (grid = range(500, 801, 500) = (500,)). The loop's line `if t < floor or len(curve) < 2: continue` gates the WHOLE call to src/sig/api.py::_stop_verdict, including its ABSOLUTE collapse arm `sep < 0.15`, which by its own arithmetic needs only one probe -- so with one probe _stop_verdict is never called at all and `verdict` stays at its initial 'budget'. Measured: a stream on which every window is identical warms to separation_final = -0.000000, far below the 0.15 threshold, and warm_up returns WarmupReport(verdict='budget') -- 'the full budget ran with no plateau'. The same stream at SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=200 (2 probes) returns verdict='collapsing' at step 400, so the mechanism is correct and only its reachability is wrong. What makes this a defect rather than a configuration note is the gate: st.gates['sig.adaptive_stop'] is correctly UNREACHABLE, but its reason sentence ends 'WHAT IS STILL LIVE ON THIS SETTING: the collapsing verdict's ABSOLUTE arm (separation below 0.15) needs only one probe, so a collapse can still be declared and sig.warmup_verdict is the surface that says so'. That sentence is false at the very defaults it is printed under, and it points the operator at sig.warmup_verdict, which reads 'budget'. This is the historical failure the module was written to remove, restored one level up: warm_up's docstring records a single-corpus run whose separation went 0.16 -> 0.05 being told it had converged, SHIFT_DIST never firing, 0 boundaries, 1 domain, and every downstream line still printing. The only surface that still carries the truth is the counter sig.warmup_separation_final (and WarmupReport.separation_final), which no clause names as the collapse signal. Fix is one line -- let the collapse test run on a curve of length 1 (or let the absolute arm run before the len(curve) < 2 guard) -- and the gate's reason then becomes true. NO WIRE IS NEEDED. Both call sites are unguarded (spine/compose.py L2047), so this is on the critical path of every fresh run.
findings.repro: cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad && timeout 500 python3 -u repro_sig.py   ->  'SIG_WARMUP=800 SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=500 -> probes=1 / separation_final = -0.000000 (collapse threshold 0.15) / verdict = budget'  and  'same stream, SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=200 (2 probes) -> verdict=collapsing'. The script boots from spine.assemble.build(environ={}), mints streams via train/api.py::streams over spine/compose.py::RNG_SUBSYSTEMS, sizes the encoder with spine/compose.py::_signature_width and ::_alphabet_size, builds the optimizer with opt/api.py::build, and passes opt=OptState.encoder exactly as spine/compose.py::compose does.

findings.detail: The counter sig.cadence_idle is ABSENT from st.counters after any run that never leaves the dense arm, which at the shipped SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=1 is every such run -- so the reading the function's own DID IT FIRE block names is a KeyError rather than a 0. The seeding is written as `st.counters.setdefault('sig.cadence_dense', dense_fires); st.counters.setdefault('sig.cadence_idle', idle_fires)` inside the ELSE branch of `if due:`, under a comment that states its purpose exactly: 'SEEDED SO A REPORT READ AFTER A RUN THAT NEVER ENTERED AN ARM SEES A ZERO AND NOT A MISSING KEY -- the same reason build() seeds the four encode counters.' At SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=1 the dense arm's period is 1, so `int(step) % 1 == 0` is true on every window, `due` is always True, the else branch never executes, and the seeding never runs. The docstring's DID IT FIRE block then names a reading that cannot be taken: 'sig.cadence_idle == 0 for a whole run means the gate never left the dense arm'. Measured: 50 dense-arm calls at defaults leave counters {'sig.cadence_checks': 50, 'sig.cadence_dense': 50} and st.counters['sig.cadence_idle'] raises KeyError. The mirror case is safe -- an idle-only run has non-due windows (period 12), so both keys get seeded -- and SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=2 also seeds both, which is why this hides everywhere except the shipped default. Note src/sig/api.py::build does NOT seed the cadence counters (it seeds only width/alphabet/encoder_built/bigram_built/the four encode counters/train_steps), so there is no second source for the key. Severity is medium and not high because st.gates['sig.cadence_idle'] IS written on every call, so the report's GATE line is correct and honest; it is the counter half of the same DID IT FIRE contract that is missing. Fix is to move the two setdefault calls above the `if due:` branch, or to seed both cadence counters in build() beside the encode counters. NO WIRE IS NEEDED.
findings.repro: cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad && timeout 500 python3 -u repro_sig.py   -> 'SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=1 (every dense check is due) after 50 dense windows: counters = {sig.cadence_checks: 50, sig.cadence_dense: 50}' then 'KeyError(sig.cadence_idle)'. Also cad2.py in the same directory shows the contrast: idle-only and SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=2 runs both seed the missing key.

findings.detail: The interface to OPT holds under a real joint call. Proven, from a spine.assemble.build() config: (a) KEY SPELLINGS MATCH -- spine/compose.py L2005-2008 passes param_groups={'base': sysm.base_params, 'encoder': list(sig_api.encoder_parameters(sig, sysm.sig))}, opt/api.py::build refuses any key that is not 'base' or 'encoder' and orders them as (('base', ...), ('encoder', ...)), and those two spellings ARE the OptState field names (Q-OPT-7). (b) THE PARAMETERS ARRIVE -- the returned list is 3 objects whose ids are exactly [id(p) for p in st.encoder.parameters()] in order, and exactly the id-set held by OptState.encoder.param_groups; none of them appears in OptState.base.param_groups, and opt.build.group_overlap = 0. (c) THEY RECEIVE A GRADIENT STEP -- one _encode_for_training forward, .backward(), OptState.encoder.step() moved emb.weight by 2.000e-3, proj.weight by 2.000e-3 and proj.bias by 2.000e-3, while the base group's parameter moved by exactly 0.0. (d) SHAPE RECORDING -- opt.build.params.encoder = 3 and param_group_shape = (('base', 1, ((3,3),)), ('encoder', 3, ((256,64),(64,64),(64,)))), so OPT's L50 resume refusal has the real live encoder shape to compare against. (e) THE RETURN TYPE IS WHAT OPT ASKED FOR -- a plain list (not a generator: OPT reads the group twice, once for the AdamW and once for _param_group_shape), and all entries are torch.nn.Parameter. (f) THE BIGRAM ARM -- returns [], SigState.encoder is a raw (512,64) Tensor and .parameters() is never called on it, opt/api.py::build accepts the empty group (AdamW over an explicit param-group dict) and records opt.build.params.encoder = 0 rather than refusing. (g) THREE-STATE GATE -- learned arm 'Gate sig.encoder_params: FIRED (3 vs 1)'; bigram arm 'UNREACHABLE (0 vs 1)' with a reason naming SIG_MODE='bigram' and saying why 0 is not a count. (h) IDEMPOTENT -- the second call site (spine/compose.py::_n_params) re-assigns the counter and re-declares the gate rather than incrementing, so calling it twice cannot inflate either. (i) LEVERS READ: mode -- exactly one lever read by AST, in both directions; WIRES READ: none, and none read.

findings.detail: Everything warm_up is contracted to consume, mutate and not mutate, checked before/after on a real config. IT USES THE NAMED FIELD: spine/compose.py L2047-2049 passes opt=sysm.optimizer.encoder, and the body touches `opt` only through zero_grad(set_to_none=True) / step() -- there is no path from it to the language model. Before/after over 800 steps at defaults: encoder emb.weight moved 0.1866, proj.weight 0.3564, proj.bias 0.0126; the base group's parameter moved 0.0; OptState.encoder.state went 0 -> 3 entries while OptState.base.state stayed 0; every encoder .grad is None afterwards (the trailing zero_grad, so the loop's first step cannot apply a warm-up gradient under a counter that says the loop trained); OPT's own counters are untouched (warm_up steps the AdamW directly, which is what SIG.train_step's docstring says is the design -- OPT.maybe_step writes lr into this optimizer and does not step it). THE CURVE IS REPLACED, NOT EXTENDED: st.warmup_curve was pre-seeded to [0.999, 0.998] and came back as exactly this call's curve, which is the resume property WarmupReport's docstring requires. All five contracted counters are written (sig.warmup_steps=800, sig.warmup_probes=1, sig.warmup_verdict, sig.warmup_separation_peak, sig.warmup_separation_final) and st.mode / st.width_units / st.alphabet_size are unchanged. THE PROBE GOES THROUGH encode(): sig.encode_calls=1 and sig.encode_windows=96 = 2 x SIG_CONTRASTIVE_BATCH, with sig.encode_width_seen=614 = st.width_units and sig.encode_width_mismatch=0, so the instrument is counted and width-asserted like every other signature. ALL FIVE ARMS OF Gate sig.adaptive_stop were exercised and each unreachable arm carries a reason naming its lever and value: SIG_MODE=bigram (UNREACHABLE 200 vs 800), SIG_WARMUP=0 (UNREACHABLE 0 vs 0), SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC=1.0 and 1.01 (UNREACHABLE 800 vs 800 / 808 vs 800), SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=500 with one probe (UNREACHABLE 200 vs 800), and SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=100 (FIRED 200 vs 800 on verdict 'plateau'). LEVERS READ names exactly the seven the body reads, in both directions, by AST: mode, warmup, warmup_min_frac, warmup_plateau_eps, warmup_probe_every, contrastive_batch, d. The three further levers reached transitively -- temp, var_weight, cov_weight via _contrastive_loss/_var_cov -- are declared on train_step, which is what the block comment above src/sig/api.py::_unit_tensor argues for and what tests/test_contract.py accepts. Every DID IT FIRE name declared is produced and nothing undeclared is produced. Separately verified: _draw_pairs and _separation index within bounds (max read index seen_units-2 in both), and the width used by both is st.width_units and nothing else.

findings.detail: THE GENERATOR: no second mint, and the fifth stream collision has not happened. The whole of src/sig contains exactly two torch.Generator constructions -- src/sig/api.py L161 (build, on the target device, `gen.manual_seed(generator.randint(0, 2**31-1))` off the handed-in stream) and L750 (warm_up, CPU, `gen.manual_seed(int(st.rng.randint(0, 2**31-1)))` where st.rng IS the same stream build was handed). Both are LOCAL torch generators seeded by one draw off the package's declared stream; neither is a new named stream. Grep over src/sig for rng_for, .spawn(, torch_generator, numpy_generator, torch.manual_seed and random. finds only two COMMENT mentions (L742 and L745) and no call. Measured across a full 800-step warm_up on a config whose streams were minted by train/api.py::streams over compose.RNG_SUBSYSTEMS: spine.rng.issued() holds the same ten names before and after, the 'sig' stream's .draws went 1 -> 2 (build's one draw plus warm_up's one), and torch's global RNG state is bit-identical before and after (torch.equal on get_rng_state()), so nothing in this package touches the global torch stream. The deliberate avoidance of st.rng.torch_generator() is correct and load-bearing: that method derives its seed from the stream's NAME, so warm_up and train_step would both receive a generator starting at the same state and draw the same windows -- correlated draws with nothing in the ledger to say so. The one consequence worth stating plainly, since it is not a defect but is a property: warm_up's local generator is seeded from the SECOND draw off the sig stream, so its window draws depend on how many draws SIG.build made first. That is deterministic under a fixed seed and confined to one package's own stream, which is exactly what spine/rng.py's design intends.
findings.repro: grep -rn "rng_for|\\.spawn\\(|torch_generator|numpy_generator|torch.manual_seed|random\\." src/sig/  -> two comment lines only, no call sites; grep -n "torch.Generator|manual_seed" src/sig/api.py -> L161/L162 and L750/L751 only. Runtime proof in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/warm.py: 'sig stream draws: 1 -> 2', 'torch GLOBAL rng state untouched: True', and rng.issued() unchanged.

findings.detail: THE ENCODER WIDTH: no live-vocabulary assumption was reintroduced by any of the three new bodies. None of encoder_parameters, warm_up or cadence_due reads a vocabulary quantity at all -- the only occurrences of 'vocab' in src/sig/api.py are in docstrings and comments, and the only Config attributes read by the three are the levers listed in their own LEVERS READ blocks plus the d_idle_cadence wire. The width comes from ONE field: src/sig/api.py::_windows_at takes `width` as an argument and its only two callers pass int(st.width_units) (via _draw_pairs) or st.width_units (via _separation); src/sig/api.py::encode asserts int(units.shape[1]) == st.width_units on every call and counts sig.encode_width_mismatch before raising. The alphabet is likewise an argument: spine/compose.py::_alphabet_size returns int(lm.vocab_slots) under space='tokens' and 256 under 'bytes', and src/sig/api.py::build passes it straight into _Encoder without consulting any live size. Proven at runtime on the token arm, which is where a live-size assumption would bite: with SIG_SPACE=tokens the encoder is built with emb.weight of shape (4096, 64) = LM.vocab_slots rows, a full warm_up over a stream whose LIVE vocabulary is 300 ids leaves emb rows at 4096 and width_units at 614, and OPT's param_group_shape records ('encoder', 3, ((4096,64),(64,64),(64,))) -- so the encoder AdamW's moment shapes are pinned to the slot ceiling and a mid-run vocabulary widen inside the ceiling cannot move them. That is the moment-shape stability SIG.build's docstring gives as the reason, and ISSUES P3-H24 from the other side.
findings.repro: cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad && python3 edge.py  -> section 'space=tokens: encoder width at the SLOT ceiling': 'LM.vocab_slots=4096  _alphabet_size(sig, lm)=4096', 'encoder emb rows = 4096 == LM.vocab_slots: True', 'warm_up over a 300-id live vocab against a 4096-row encoder -> plateau 40 steps', 'emb rows still 4096 ; width_units still 614'.

findings.detail: Apart from the counter-seeding defect recorded above, cadence_due matches its docstring clause by clause. THE WIRE IS READ, NOT THE LEVER: `idle_period = int(sig.d_idle_cadence)` and the observed idle firing gap tracks the wire across three settings -- SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=1 gives gap 12 (wire 12, lever 12), =3 gives gap 18 (wire 18, lever still 12), =10 gives gap 60 (wire 60, lever still 12). That is P1-H53 actually landed rather than asserted: change the dense cadence and the idle cadence follows. THE CLOCKS ARE TYPED AND CROSS-KIND ARGUMENTS RAISE: both incoming values go through U.Windows(), so step_windows=Steps(4) and step_windows=Flushes(4) both raise UnitError('cannot build Windows from Steps'/'from Flushes'), as does windows_since_boundary=Steps(10). The arm selection `since < dense_for` is a Windows-against-Windows comparison, and `int(step) % period` is a same-kind modulo through Clock.__index__ (units.py declares __index__ exists 'so range(), slicing and % work'), not a cross-kind conversion -- there is no inline // or * between kinds anywhere in the function. Bare ints are accepted, which is correct: that is the spelling Config hands back for all 35 clock-unit levers, and the docstring's claim is specifically that a Steps is refused. THREE-STATE GATES, ALL EXERCISED: SIG_MODE=bigram gives both arms UNREACHABLE with a reason naming SIG_MODE, SIG_TRAIN_EVERY, SIG_TRAIN_EVERY_IDLE and SIG_DENSE_WINDOW and saying 'a count of 0 fires here is not a cadence that declined to fire'; SIG_DENSE_WINDOW=0 gives sig.cadence_dense UNREACHABLE ('no window count is below 0, so the gate is stuck open on the throttled arm for the whole run') while sig.cadence_idle correctly reads 'armed, did not fire'; at defaults both read FIRED with the fire counts in the reason. The printed pair is (this arm's period vs SIG_DENSE_WINDOW) on both gates and not the last call's windows_since_boundary, which is what stops a per-window gate from printing whatever the last window happened to be. LEVERS READ names exactly mode, train_every, train_every_idle, dense_window and WIRES READ names exactly d_idle_cadence -- both exact in both directions by AST. All three DID IT FIRE names are produced. NO WIRE WAS SPENT: d_idle_cadence is a LOCAL coupling (both endpoints are SIG's) and books no ledger edge, so the budget is still 23 of 25.

findings.detail: The `floor >= budget` arm of Gate sig.adaptive_stop ends its reason with 'This is the untrippable-guard shape the fraction was introduced to make unrepresentable, and it is reachable again only above SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC=1.0.' The boundary is off by one value: the arm is selected by `elif floor >= budget`, so at SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC=1.0 exactly, floor = int(1.0 * 800) = 800 >= 800 and the gate is ALREADY unreachable -- verified, the run prints 'Gate sig.adaptive_stop: UNREACHABLE (800 vs 800)'. The sentence should read 'at or above 1.0'. This matters only because the sentence is the reader's instruction for how to get the mechanism back, and following it literally (setting exactly 1.0) leaves the stop still unreachable. Related and also low: SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC is declared with unit FRACTION 0..1 but a Lever has no range facility, so a negative fraction yields a negative floor and silently makes the stop eligible from the first comparable probe with no gate saying so -- there is no refusal for it the way build() refuses SIG_MODE=bigram at width 1.

findings.detail: The `period < 1` refusal is evaluated before the `mode != 'learned'` branch, so SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=0 raises ValueError on the FIRST window of a SIG_MODE=bigram run -- on an arm where the same function's own gate reason states 'SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=0, SIG_TRAIN_EVERY_IDLE=12 and SIG_DENSE_WINDOW=400 are inert on this arm'. The message names a failure that cannot occur there: `due = bool(mode == 'learned' and int(step) % period == 0)` short-circuits on the bigram arm, so the 'modulo by zero' it describes is never evaluated. Two smaller notes in the same family: (a) the refusal fires per-window rather than at build, so an incoherent cadence lever takes down the run at the first loop window instead of at startup, where SIG.build already refuses SIG_MODE=bigram at width_units=1; (b) the refusal message renders the message-only lever read (`lever_idle`) correctly, so the operator does get both the lever and the wire value. Reported as low because loud refusal of an incoherent value is defensible and nothing is silently wrong -- the finding is the disagreement between the refusal and the gate reason printed by the same function.

findings.detail: WarmupReport.verdict and the counter sig.warmup_verdict both read 'budget' on two arms where no step ran at all. warm_up's docstring defines 'budget' as 'the full budget ran with no plateau'. Measured: SIG_MODE=bigram returns verdict='budget' with steps=0 and probes=0 against SIG_WARMUP=800, and SIG_WARMUP=0 returns verdict='budget' with steps=0. The initialiser `curve, steps, probes, verdict = [], 0, 0, 'budget'` is simply not overwritten when the `if mode == 'learned'` block is skipped. This is bounded rather than serious for two reasons: WarmupReport declares verdict as one of exactly three strings, so there is no fourth spelling available without a record-type change; and Gate sig.adaptive_stop carries the honest reading on both arms -- 'SIG_MODE=bigram: ... SIG_WARMUP=800 is inert on this arm and sig.warmup_steps is 0 for that reason, not because a stop fired at step 0' and 'SIG_WARMUP=0: there is no pre-loop budget'. A composition root reading the GATE is told the truth; a root reading only WarmupReport.verdict -- which the record's own docstring calls 'what the composition root has to act on itself' -- is told the budget was spent. Recording it so the owner can rule on whether the record needs a fourth verdict or whether the gate is the intended surface; it is not something to fix by narrowing anything.

unfinished.detail: src/opt/api.py::build constructs the encoder AdamW with lr=OPT_LR, and OPT.maybe_step -- which is what normally writes the scheduled rate into this optimizer's param groups -- has not run when spine/compose.py calls warm_up. So all 800 warm-up steps run at full peak OPT_LR with none of the linear warmup or cosine the loop gets, and OPT's counters record none of them (opt.step and opt.encoder_steps_here are both still 0 after warm_up, measured). SIG.train_step's docstring is explicit that SIG never names a learning rate and that stepping the encoder AdamW directly is the design, so nothing here contradicts the contract; what is undecided is whether the pre-loop budget should be spent at peak. Recording it rather than treating it as a defect.
